correctness.rationale: With flat whole-profile Poisson resets, the stationary age is Exp(r) and point evaluations are conditionally Gaussian. The spatial heat-kernel resolvent gives covariance D exp(-ell sqrt(s/(2nu)))/sqrt(2nu s), with s=r+2mu. Exponential-age integration of the squared error-function conditional variance gives K=(12/pi)y atan(1/y)-3. Its derivative is strictly positive for all y>1 and endpoint values give exactly the open range. The inverse explicitly reconstructs positive mu,r,D for every admissible observable triple, so existence and uniqueness are both proved. Five independent numerical quadratures and inverse tests passed; boundary cases are excluded and not inferred from finite tests.

value.rationale: Two distinct physical mechanisms, restoring pinning and global restarting, both suppress low-frequency fluctuations and cannot be distinguished from spatial covariance alone, since it depends on r+2mu. The exact fourth-moment law separates their ratio and restores identifiability; noise intensity is recovered from variance, yielding a natural full-range three-parameter inverse theorem with sharp image inequalities. This is a motivated structural distinction between equilibrium-like pinning and nonequilibrium resetting, not merely a numerical fit or small parameter optimization.
